results.strategy_description:
The fund aims to deliver consistent alpha in a passive world, through market neutral strategies with no or low sensitivity to traditional market movements. Two strategies with complementary risk profiles are implemented through an investment process relying on quantitative opportunities detection combined with a fundamental selection overlay: 1. Index rebalancing: large trades coming from passive investments lead to price spread opportunities; 2. Relative value: large inflows/outflows coming from passive investments lead to valuation spread opportunities.

This is a highly differentiated product, with limited equivalent offerings in the market for these strategies, in a daily liquid UCITS fund. The approach on these strategies is also unique, with more than 20 years of track record, and a consistent implementation across markets and regions. The strategies are benefiting from the growth of passive management (over 50% of the total equity funds AUM in the US, reaching 40% in Europe) and its impact on stock prices, volatility and liquidity, thus providing a strong tailwind.

results.management_company_description: 9 Masts (“9M”) are pioneers of relative value & arbitrage strategies in Asia. In 2010 they launched their flagship multi-strategy fund with the goal of providing investors with market neutral alpha. The team trades in and across a variety of asset classes including credit, equities, convertible bonds, FX and interest rates products to generate uncorrelated and market agnostic return streams. The investment process is repeatable and is based on the overlap of fundamental, statistical, and technical factors, which is balanced with robust risk management. The partners have worked together since 2007 and, together with employees, represent one of the largest investors within the fund. 9M is headquartered in Hong Kong.
results.strategy_description:
Nine Masts deploys market neutral, relative value strategies with a focus on the Asia Pacific region through liquid trading activities predominantly across equity, credit, futures and volatility asset classes. The team aims to capitalize from the frequent dislocations that arise in the target investment markets, by deploying an interlinked fundamental, statistical and technical approach. The portfolio is liquid and mostly comprised of equities, bonds, futures and derivatives.

Investment selection and sizing is undertaken by way of qualitative and quantitative capital allocation, portfolio construction and risk management techniques. Selection is focused on targeting favourable asymmetric expected return profiles with minimal market correlation, through well-developed investment theses. The deepening and broadening capital markets in the region, including the latest developments in China, continue to offer high quality risk/return adjusted opportunities. The portfolio is primarily made up of, but not limited to: relative value investments; curve and basis trading; index, volatility and convertible bond arbitrage; capital structure and equity vs credit trading; fungible and non-fungible equity strategies; quantitative and systematic activities.

results.management_company_description: EJF Capital LLC (“EJF”) is an SEC-registered alternative asset management firm headquartered outside of Washington, D.C. EJF manages approximately $5.4 billion* of hedge fund assets, separately managed accounts, and private equity assets, including $2.9 billion* of CDO assets through affiliates. EJF currently employs approximately 45 professionals across two offices globally (Arlington, Virginia · London, England). Since its inception, EJF has focused on anticipating and interpreting the consequences of regulatory change within the broader financials sector.  *Firm AUM as of 12/31/25 includes $151.6 million of uncalled capital.
results.strategy_description:
The EJF Financial Services Fund (the “Fund”) utilizes a catalyst-driven approach to opportunistically deploy capital in primarily U.S.-based equity securities focused in the banking or related financials sector. The Fund seeks to capitalize on inefficiencies and dislocations resulting from structural changes within complex, niche financial markets. EJF’s ability to execute the strategy is driven by our capital markets and specialty finance transaction experience, and enhanced by our substantial long-term relationships with corporate management teams and our deep understanding of their financial institutions.

EJF believes that the financial services industry is undergoing a sea change when it comes to technology and digitization. Post the COVID-19 pandemic, banks are increasingly focused on technology as a mechanism to increase productivity, reach new customers, preserve their core businesses, and make informed decisions on business expansion and capital allocation.  Fintech has numerous potential applications including technology that helps banks streamline operations so banks can do more with less human involvement, underwrite and manage loans, and more efficiently manage anti-money laundering compliance and cybersecurity risk. Fundamentally, EJF believes that the banking sector as a whole is well capitalized and credit quality remains strong.  Net interest margin (“NIM”) expansion will be a tailwind to earnings power in the near-term as the U.S. Federal Reserve (the “Fed”) is expected to increase rates throughout 2022 and early 2023 to combat elevated levels of inflation.  Overall, EJF believes that the discounted values of the financial services sector create an unusual opportunity to extract value in small and mid-cap banking companies, specialty finance and financial technology companies.  

The Fund invests primarily in:
U.S. community & regional banks benefiting from regulatory changes
U.S. specialty finance and financial technology companies
Other U.S. financial services companies
results.region_exposure_description: The Fund’s geographical focus has primarily been on North American assets, but also has had a minority of its exposure to European opportunities. The Fund has considered and will continue to consider investments in other areas so long as they fit within the Fund’s strategy.

In January 2022, EJF hired a third-party consultant to assist with the broadening of its policy and DEI goals and to ensure best practices are adhered to.  EJF is committed to further building out its DEI program and as such is exploring different ways in which it can further educate its employee base through third-party training which it launched in August 2022.  Additionally, EJF has committed to having a representative sit on the Milken Institutes newly established DEI in Asset Management Council that will work toward promoting diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives in the asset management industry.

(the “Fund”) seeks to provide a carry neutral "tail hedge" through a portfolio primarily consisting of long and short credit default swap ("CDS") positions with the aim of achieving strong absolute returns during periods of market stress. The long portfolio is expected to be comprised of companies that have historically demonstrated minimal spread widening in past periods of market stress, while the short portfolio will be comprised of companies that have historically demonstrated heightened spread widening in past periods of market stress. Generally, the spreads of both sides of the portfolio will on average be similar to each other during normal market conditions. A "tail hedge" is designed to hedge against tail risk posed by events that, while rare, can significantly and adversely affect markets. Through the use of the long portfolio, the Fund seeks to neutralize the cost of the "tail hedge". Saba believes that by using proprietary tools and blending fundamental credit analysis with trade analytics, it can establish an effective tail hedge.

results.strategy_description:
Sculptor Multi-Strategy Fund is a global multi-strategy best-ideas fund that seeks to generate strong and consistent risk-adjusted returns across market cycles, with a focus on risk management and capital preservation. The Fund identifies high conviction investments across the depth and breadth of global equity, credit and convertible securities and derivatives markets. Capital is flexibly allocated to the most attractive opportunities whenever and wherever they arise. This unconstrained approach is key to the Fund’s ability to deliver excess return over time. The Fund targets net returns of approximately 500-700 basis points in excess of the risk-free rate with limited volatility and low beta to global equity markets.

The Fund has a primary focus on idiosyncratic opportunities where return drivers are less sensitive to market direction. These investments tend to arise where intermediate- or long-term value is obscured by attributes such as complexity, corporate events, technical dislocations, forced buying and selling, or market misunderstandings. Additionally, the Fund has the flexibility to tactically alter its overall risk profile when the investment team believes that broader market dislocations have created asymmetric upside or downside. Sculptor’s investment team works to achieve the Fund’s objectives via rigorous bottom-up fundamental analysis, a dynamic approach to capital allocation, and a sophisticated and fully integrated risk management strategy.
results.region_exposure_description:
Given the Fund’s unconstrained approach, it does not have static or pre-determined geographic, sector, or asset class allocations or limits. However, exposures are naturally limited (and need to be appropriate) so that the Fund is able to meet its contractual liquidity and expected return profile of equity like returns with limited volatility and low beta to global equity markets. These factors naturally constrain how large our exposure can be to any specific factor, geography, asset class, instrument type, sector, or industry. The CIO, with the support of the Risk and Portfolio Committees, actively monitors a wide range of portfolio risks and dynamically adjusts the portfolio in real time.

In most cases, the long position is a security which is readily convertible into the underlying short position.

results.management_company_description:
Axebrook Capital LLP ("Axebrook") is a London-based partnership established by founder and CIO Jack Land.  Axebrook is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority to act as an Alternative Investment Fund Manager.  

Prior to Axebrook, Jack was at York Capital Management ("York"), where since July 2020 he was lead portfolio manager for the Axebrook Credit Alpha Fund ("ACA" or the "Fund", formerly known as the York Global Credit Income Fund).  With effect from 1 February 2022, Axebrook replaced York as investment manager of the Fund.  The master and feeder fund vehicles remain unchanged and existing investors fully consented to the spinoff. Day 1 capital was in excess of $100 million, with substantial support via a seeding arrangement with York affiliated investors. 

The Axebrook team was built up during 2021 and brings with it significant industry experience.
results.strategy_description:
ACA is a liquid credit fund investing primarily in corporate credit in the US and Europe (bonds, loans and CDS), both long and short. This absolute return strategy is based on fundamental, bottoms-up research, with an event-driven tilt.  Axebrook believes that corporate credit markets are inherently inefficient due to various systemic factors (e.g. sharp decline in broker dealer holdings post 2008, limited “electronification” in credit markets, the rise of CLOs and ETFs, non-economic buy and sell decisions driven by ratings agency actions, etc), and aims to generate high risk-adjusted returns at all points in the credit cycle by exploiting mispriced risk in these markets. 

The Firm will apply an active trading strategy and vary its net exposure to manage risk throughout the cycle.  Portfolio construction will typically consist of 40-50 long positions and 10-20 short positions, with a targeted gross exposure of 100-200% and a net exposure of 40-60%.  The strategy’s short book is comprised of single name alpha shorts as well as overlay hedges (both risk and rates) that seek to minimize volatility and drawdown risk.

The Fund is structured as a Cayman master feeder with an onshore and offshore feeder. Liquidity terms are quarterly with 90 days notice.  There are no investor level or fund level gates.  The Fund will have two share classes, a Founders Class and a Standard Class, which differ as to lock up term and management fees and performance fees charged.
